title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch
slides: Can a four-month-old startup be worth $1 billion?
Town raised a unicorn round just months after launch
But its AI assistant does something most rivals avoid
Teams using it now face a key tradeoff they underestimated
Test one real workflow before your competitor does
thread_text:
1. Four months to $1B?

Town launched its AI assistant just months ago and already hit unicorn status. But the real story isn't the valuation — it's what the assistant refuses to do.

2. The feature rivals skip

Most AI assistants try to do everything. Town's deliberately limits its scope, avoiding the feature bloat that competitors pile on. That restraint is exactly what attracted investors.

3. A hidden tradeoff

Teams adopting Town now face a choice they didn't see coming: the assistant's narrow focus means you must adapt your workflow to it, not the other way around. That constraint cuts both ways.

4. Underestimated cost

The tradeoff isn't just technical — it's operational. Early users report that fitting Town into existing processes takes more effort than expected, eating into the time savings it promises.

5. Test before you commit

Take one real workflow — say, drafting a client email or summarizing a report — and run it through Town. If you haven't done that, don't sign off until you do.

instagram.caption:
Four months to a $1 billion valuation — before most teams have even tried the product.

Town just hit unicorn status with an AI assistant that deliberately does less than its rivals. It skips the feature bloat competitors pile on, and that restraint is what pulled in investors. 🤔

The catch: adopting it means reshaping your workflow around its narrow focus, not the other way. Early users say fitting it in takes more effort than expected.

If you write or publish for a living, that setup cost lands on your daily output.

Before you commit, run one real task through it — a client email, a report summary. Have you actually tested it, or just read the pitch? 👀
